name: Determining When a Student Fails a Course (Case 3)
description: Construct a program that determines whether a student fails the course based on the inputs that it receives from the instructor. The student fails the course if his/her score is not above the class average.

comments.content: We need to read and process the values that the instructor enters. To read the input values from the instructor, we need to define a Scanner object.

We can create a Scanner object using the operator new, as shown in this statement. The System.in object represents the standard input stream, which by default is the keyboard. It tells the java compiler that the input will be provided through keyboard.
We prompt the instructor to enter the student's score.
We need to read the student's score that the instructor enters and store it in a variable. We read the student's score by calling the nextInt() method because this input is an integer.
Note that if the instructor provides a non-integer number, an exception will be thrown because the input type is inconsistent with the expected data type, i.e., int.
We prompt the instructor to enter the class average.
We need to read the class average that the instructor enters and store it in a variable. We read the class average by calling the nextInt() method because this input is an integer.
Note that if the instructor provides a non-integer number, an exception will be thrown because the input type is inconsistent with the expected data type, i.e., int.
We close the scanner as we do not want to process any input from the instructor in the rest of the program.

We could check whether a student fails the course by inverting the condition that tests whether the student passes the course. In other words, we could invert the condition that tests if the student's score is above the class average. Note that we invert the condition by using ! (not) operator.
The ! operator takes a single condition and evaluates to true if that condition is false and to false if the condition is true.
This statement prints true/false depending on whether the student fails the course. The printed value is followed by an end-of-line character in the end.
